public_reference.summary: A legacy ShiVa tutorial describes integrating native callbacks by changing the native client project and registering AI-event hooks. It is contextual background for the native-client integration boundary, not proof this compiled Dungeon Quest build exposes the same editable project or callback ABI.

next_gates: Locate the exact-build S3DX/AIFunction declaration and its callback/user-data layout from an authorized matching SDK/header or source project.
Determine whether the application provides an authorized native initialization hook for registering and unregistering a client function and establish callback lifetime/thread rules.
Use a benign no-side-effect test callback in an isolated development build to prove registration, invocation and unregister behavior before considering any game-state handler.
Only after the native callback contract is proven should a bounded, allow-listed adapter be designed; preserve the runtime read-back, save/reload, recovery and regression gates.
scope_limitations: Static ARM64 disassembly only; no live invocation, injection, APK mutation or gameplay mutation was performed.
The public tutorial is older and describes an author-controlled ShiVa Android Studio project; it is not a guarantee of compatibility with Dungeon Quest's packaged runtime.
S3DX::AIFunction is accepted as an opaque pointer by the exported registration entrypoint; its exact layout and ABI have not been recovered in this pass.
A registered client function API does not itself prove that the packaged game contains a hook to register a new function or that an arbitrary HUD action can call it.
The catalog remains fail-closed; no cheat route is assigned or runtime verified.
